summary: Round r1 (restricted network). Question: Nepal's petroleum import bill as a share of total imports and its price sensitivity. No value was retrieved; the share and the sensitivity are PENDING. Primary documents were located: NRB Current Macroeconomic and Financial Situation releases (FY2024/25 annual and FY2025/26 monthly cumulative, major-imports table), Department of Customs Foreign Trade Statistics (HS 27 by product and partner), Nepal Oil Corporation import/sales, pricing-period profit-and-loss and publications pages, and international price series (World Bank Pink Sheet and CMO, IMF PCPS, IEA Oil Market Report, EIA STEO). Method designed: share = HS 27 (or NRB 'petroleum products') import value / total merchandise imports, Nepal FY; sensitivity decomposed into (i) international benchmark to IOC invoice price (via NOC pricing-period sheets), (ii) invoice price to import bill (price x volume, with a volume elasticity), (iii) NPR/INR/USD exchange-rate effect, and (iv) invoice price to retail price (automatic pricing formula, taxes and discretionary overrides). Search results indicate a 2026 Middle East oil supply shock (IEA OMR July and September 2026, NRB FY2025/26 releases); it is unverified and flagged to Agents 15 and 28 because it bears on S01, S04 and S10.

findings.claim: Petroleum products import value and share of total merchandise imports, FY2024/25 (and FY2015/16-FY2024/25 history).
findings.note: Need NRB CME major-imports table (petroleum products, NPR) and total imports, plus customs HS 27 totals; keep both values and reconcile (NRB BoP-adjusted vs customs basis).

findings.claim: Petroleum products import value and share, FY2025/26 (latest cumulative months) - captures the 2026 price shock.
findings.note: NRB CME ten/eleven/twelve-month FY2025/26 releases; customs monthly FTS.

findings.claim: Import volumes by product (petrol, diesel, kerosene, ATF, LPG) and NOC import cost, by FY.
findings.note: NOC import-and-sales tables (kl, tonnes; NPR); customs HS 2710/2711 quantity and value.

findings.claim: Supplier and route concentration of petroleum supply (IOC share; pipeline vs road tanker by entry point).
findings.note: NOC annual report / supply agreement; feeds 16B CM-05 and SPOF-01.

findings.claim: Automatic pricing formula: components (IOC invoice price, customs duty, excise, infrastructure/pollution levies, VAT, NOC margin, other funds) and revision frequency; history of suspensions or overrides.
findings.note: NOC pricing directives and pricing-period profit-and-loss sheets; the formula text itself is the evidence required. Media reports (leads L19, L20) indicate periods when automatic adjustment was suspended - verify from NOC decisions.

findings.claim: Pass-through coefficient from international benchmark (Brent / Singapore products) to IOC invoice price to Nepal, and to Nepal retail price.
findings.note: Regress NOC per-period invoice prices on benchmark prices converted at the same-period INR/USD; retail prices on invoice prices; requires the NOC time series of per-period cost sheets.

findings.claim: Sensitivity of the FY petroleum import bill to a benchmark crude price change (NPR per USD/bbl, and percent of total imports).
findings.note: Computed only after pass-through and volume elasticity are estimated from retrieved data; will be labelled estimate with observation ids.

findings.claim: International crude and product price path, monthly 2019-2026 and forecast 2026-2027, re-aggregated to Nepal FY.
findings.note: Monthly Pink Sheet historical Excel, IMF PCPS; IEA OMR/World Bank CMO for forecast ranges; EIA STEO as alternative.

findings.claim: 2026 oil-market disruption (Middle East / US-Iran impasse) - dating, magnitude and duration as recorded by IEA OMR and World Bank CMO.
findings.note: Retrieve OMR July and September 2026 and CMO April 2026; record as dated event observations before any scenario use.

findings.claim: Petroleum share of imports is defined on Nepal FY (mid-July) using the numerator and denominator from the same publisher and same basis; the NRB and customs bases are reported separately and never mixed.

Calendar-month international prices are re-aggregated to Nepal FY by averaging the twelve months from mid-July (approximated by August-July or July-June with the choice documented) before entering the model.

LPG and ATF are treated as separate products from petrol/diesel/kerosene because their invoice-price revision cycle and benchmark (e.g. Saudi CP for LPG) differ; the benchmark mapping is to be confirmed from NOC documents.

data_gaps: All empirical values (import value, share, volumes, pricing components, pass-through) - no primary document could be downloaded in r1.
Department of Customs FTS books for FY2023/24, FY2024/25 and FY2025/26 not yet located (only FY2022/23 book lead and a secondary media pointer).
NOC time series of per-pricing-period IOC invoice prices: availability of back history on noc.org.np/fortnightly unknown.
IOC export price formula to Nepal (benchmark, premium, freight components) - not public to our knowledge; may be available only in NOC board documents or IOC-NOC agreement.
Singapore product benchmarks (MOPS) are licensed (Platts); the IEA OMR subscription tables may also be licensed. Public proxies: Pink Sheet crude, EIA product spot prices.
Storage/stockholding days of cover by product (NOC) - not located.
Web search budget was exhausted before searches for NOC annual report PDFs and customs FY2024/25 FTS could be completed.

assumptions.text: Share of imports uses Nepal FY and a single publisher per ratio (NRB or customs); both reported with methodological notes.
Import-bill sensitivity is decomposed into price pass-through, volume response and exchange rate; the three effects are kept separate (CLAUDE.md rule 6).
NPR/INR peg is treated as fixed for pass-through estimation; NPR/USD movements therefore follow INR/USD. To be checked against NRB exchange-rate series.
Media reports are used only as pointers to official decisions, never as evidence.

challenges.text: EXP-05 methodological note should add that retail pass-through is discretionary (automatic pricing has reportedly been suspended at times - leads L19/L20, to be verified from NOC); NOC losses/fund drawdowns then become a fiscal channel rather than a CPI channel. Suggest a fiscal-contingent-liability attribute for EXP-05.

X06 source assignment should add wb_pinksheet (now in catalog) and name the product benchmark issue: IOC invoices are reportedly linked to Singapore product prices (MOPS, licensed), not crude; a crude-only series will misstate pass-through, especially during diesel-crack spikes reported in 2026.

EIA (US Energy Information Administration) STEO is not in the source catalog; propose adding as tier 4. Kathmandu Post and other media have no catalog id; propose a 'media_pointer' class that can never back a fact.

Escalation: search results (IEA OMR July/September 2026; NRB FY2025/26 releases) indicate a major 2026 oil price shock tied to Middle East disruption. If verified, it changes the baseline for S01, S04 and S10 (import bill, reserves, CPI, NOC finances).

Escalation for red-team: the 2026 oil shock plus single-supplier (IOC) dependence may be a joint geopolitical exposure; please review whether scenario S10 assumes supplier continuity during a regional supply disruption.

uncertainty: High: no value retrieved. Structural uncertainties once data arrive: (i) NRB vs customs coverage and valuation basis for petroleum imports; (ii) IOC invoice formula is not public, so pass-through must be estimated empirically and may vary by product and period; (iii) discretionary suspension of automatic pricing breaks the retail pass-through relation; (iv) the 2026 price shock may place current values outside the historical range used for estimation, so linear sensitivities may understate effects.

fuel_import_sensitivity.question: Petroleum import bill as share of total imports, and its price sensitivity

import_share.definition: petroleum products import value / total merchandise imports, Nepal FY

volumes_by_product.unit: kilolitres / tonnes (no code in units.py - see challenge 00A in 22B)

pricing_formula.content_required: NOC automatic pricing system rules: invoice price basis, tax and levy stack, margin, revision frequency, override/suspension record

pass_through_benchmark_to_invoice.method: time-series regression of NOC per-period invoice price on benchmark price x INR/USD, by product

pass_through_invoice_to_retail.method: per-period comparison of invoice and retail prices with override periods flagged

import_bill_elasticity_to_crude.method: d(import bill)/d(benchmark) = volume x pass-through x FX, plus estimated volume elasticity; reported as NPR bn per USD/bbl and as percentage-point change in import share

international_price_path.series: Pink Sheet monthly Brent/Dubai/average crude; IMF PCPS APSP; IEA OMR and World Bank CMO forecast narratives; EIA STEO
international_price_path.period_basis: calendar months, re-aggregated to Nepal FY
